To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the European Space Agency and the European Union have a common objective to develop a European space policy and to implement it through a common European space programme, and that (ii) the European Space Policy should be implemented through the European Space Programme, which is based on a coherent European space procurement law and policy for the space sector.
A coherent European procurement law and policy for the space sector requires a Third Way that is both coherent and flexible.
The Third Way in European Space procurement is the way to go.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: The legal and policy framework of public procurement in the European Union and in the European Space Agency; The specific features of the space market and their implications for the procurement policy of the European Union, the European Space Agency and their Member States; A toolbox of policy instruments that are available to the European Union, European Space Agency and Member States in order to achieve their policy objectives; A discussion of the legal and policy implications of the use of Extra-Procurement instruments; A proposal for a

a number of issues, such as the need to develop a coherent European procurement law and policy, the need to develop an integrated approach to public procurement in the European space sector, the need to identify and develop a toolbox for space sector procurement and the need to develop and implement a Third Way in European procurement.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a coherent European space procurement law and policy is needed and that the Third Way provides an appropriate framework.

the European Union should take over the European Space Agency's procurement policy and practice in the area of launchers, while the European Space Agency should take over the procurement of space systems and services.

the European Space Agency and the European Union should continue to cooperate in space procurement and that the European Commission should take the initiative in the development and implementation of a coherent European space procurement framework.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Third Way is a toolbox of procurement and nonprocurement instruments that can be used in the European space sector to achieve policy objectives, such as the development of a European space industry and the provision of space services.
we have developed a toolbox for European space procurement that provides a coherent framework for the European space sector.
we have developed a toolbox that is based on the principle of coherence between the EU and the ESA legal frameworks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a coherent European procurement law and policy for the space sector is achievable, if policy-makers are willing to take the necessary steps.
a European space sector requires European procurement rules and policies.
the European Union and ESA should be able to cooperate on the basis of a coherent European procurement law and policy for the space sector.
